Hi Laura — thanks for sending these over and for the clear summary. Looping in our sales and legal leads to respond with a practical compromise.

Quick, actionable summary from Redwood's side (high level):
- Notice window: we can shorten to a 45-day notice window (from discovery) with an evidence submission window of 30 days. The additional 15 days are necessary to triage engineering logs and reproduce the issue if it relates to model outputs.
- Cure: we are willing to accept a 30-day cure period once evidence is provided.
- Defense/control: Redwood needs the right to assume defense for third-party IP claims where Redwood's model or code is alleged to be the proximate cause. For AI-output claims (customer prompts + customer data), we propose a shared-control model: Redwood can participate and, if we assume defense, we will control but with material settlement limits requiring mutual consent for settlements above $100k.
- Scope: Redwood proposes to limit indemnity to proven third-party IP infringement (not general product performance or customer use cases) and to exclude claims arising from modifications by the customer or third-party integrations not provided by Redwood.

We will follow up with formal redlines from legal (cc'd). If Nimbus can accept the 45/30/30 split above, we can present a tracked redline for the MSA and a short Order Form addendum to close procurement.

Next steps:
1) Kimberly will send tracked redlines with suggested language for defense control and evidence requirements.
2) Sales (Ben) to confirm commercial cap options in case procurement asks for a cap.
3) If Nimbus prefers, we can propose a mutual triage process and evidence checklist to standardize SLA handling.

Best,

Hannah / Ben — see my legal note below and attached tracked redlines. I preserved the commercial compromises Hannah proposed but tightened the operational language so we don't end up with an open-ended exposure. Key points in the attached redlines:

- Notice & Evidence: replace Nimbus's unilateral 30/30 with: (a) Customer must provide written notice promptly upon becoming aware, but in any event within 45 days of discovery; (b) Customer must produce a good-faith evidence packet within 30 days of notice specifying the alleged claim, affected content, and reproducible steps/logs where applicable; (c) Redwood has 30 days after receipt of the evidence packet to investigate and propose remediation.

- Defense / Settlement: Redwood will have the right to assume defense with counsel of our choosing for third-party IP infringement claims where the alleged infringement relates to Redwood-owned model weights, code, or training data demonstrably used to generate the infringing output. If Redwood assumes defense, settlements require Redwood's consent; if Customer controls defense, Redwood will provide reasonable cooperation and reimbursement for settlement amounts allocated to Redwood. For settlements exceeding $100,000 attributable to Redwood, mutual written consent is required.

- Scope exclusions: carve out claims caused by (i) customer prompt engineering or instructions that intentionally infringe, (ii) customer-modified models or third-party integrations, (iii) open-source components subject to their own license terms (where indemnity already exists).

- Cap considerations: recommend we offer a capped indemnity for third-party IP claims tied to the Order Form value (e.g., lesser of $5M or 10x ARR for a given Order Form), but keep an exceptions bucket for willful infringement. Commercial team to confirm the numbers.

- Evidence & Escalation: add an exhibit listing minimum evidence (sample inputs/outputs, timestamps, hashes, relevant model id/version, prompt context). Also propose a 3-way monthly sync for escalated claims to keep both sides aligned on timing and remediation.

I attached a tracked redline with suggested language — please review and let me know if we should hard-code the $100k settlement threshold or make it negotiable.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
